what: S04b's 'bumper backs away' sequence (web/host/tests/damage.test.mjs) on the sim alone, with the input timing of a live eris run that tipped the car (its clip replayed natively: the same DRIVE values, tick for tick, 85 ticks earlier because the host's car spawned at tick 85). A Cruz Missile rolls on at 0.37 throttle to about 6 m/s, coasts, loses its front bumper (health 0), brakes to a stop (0.72 brake), and backs away on a 0.32 brake pull. It must back away (reversing at 2 to 8 m/s by the end) on four wheels, upright, with no wreck. Before the suspension rays learned to ignore a solid that holds their origin, the fallen bumper lay across the front-left wheel arch, that wheel's ray read it as ground at distance 0 (full suspension force, the contact point rising with the car) and the car crept up and rolled to upY 0.49 in 15 s.
